title: “Neither shall they shave their heads, nor suffer their locks to grow long; they shall only poll their heads” — Brenton’s Greek prints “nor strip their hair bare; they shall cover their heads”
summary: In the KJV of Ezekiel 44:20 the priests do not shave their heads or let the locks grow long and only poll them. Brenton’s Greek has οὐ ψιλώσουσι, “they shall not strip bare”, for the hair, and καλύπτοντες καλύψουσιν τὰς κεφαλὰς, “covering they shall cover their heads”.
text: KJV Ezekiel 44:20: “Neither shall they shave their heads, nor suffer their locks to grow long; they shall only poll their heads.” Hebrew (WLC) 44:20: וְרֹאשָׁם֙ לֹ֣א יְגַלֵּ֔חוּ וּפֶ֖רַע לֹ֣א יְשַׁלֵּ֑חוּ כָּסֹ֥ום יִכְסְמ֖וּ אֶת־רָאשֵׁיהֶֽם׃ Brenton’s Greek 44:20: Καὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν οὐ ξυρήσονται, καὶ τὰς κόμας αὐτῶν οὐ ψιλώσουσι, καλύπτοντε καλύψουσιν τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν. [And they shall not shave their heads, nor strip their hair bare; covering they shall cover their heads] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK44.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/44/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK44.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted has כָּסוֹם יִכְסְמוּ אֶת־רָאשֵׁיהֶם, “they shall surely trim their heads”, with a verb the KJV renders “poll” (cut short). It also has וּפֶרַע לֹא יְשַׁלֵּחוּ, “and they shall not let the locks go free”. The Greek printed at the same verse has καλύπτω, “to cover”, in place of a verb of cutting, and a verb for baring the hair in place of letting it grow. title: “Toward the east country, and go down into the desert” — Brenton’s Greek prints “into Galilee… and went down to Arabia”
summary: In the KJV of Ezekiel 47:8 the waters of the temple river flow out toward the east country and go down into the desert. Brenton’s Greek has εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν τὴν πρὸς ἀνατολὰς, καὶ κατέβαινεν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἀραβίαν, “into Galilee, the one toward the east… and went down to Arabia”, with two proper names.
text: KJV Ezekiel 47:8: “Then said he unto me, These waters issue out toward the east country, and go down into the desert, and go into the sea: which being brought forth into the sea, the waters shall be healed.” Hebrew (WLC) 47:8: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י הַמַּ֤יִם הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ יֹוצְאִ֗ים אֶל־הַגְּלִילָה֙ הַקַּדְמֹונָ֔ה וְיָרְד֖וּ עַל־הָֽעֲרָבָ֑ה וּבָ֣אוּ הַיָּ֔מָּה אֶל־הַיָּ֥מָּה הַמּֽוּצָאִ֖ים [וְנִרְפְּאוּ כ] (וְנִרְפּ֥וּ ק) הַמָּֽיִם׃ Brenton’s Greek 47:8: Καὶ εἶπε πρὸν μὲ, τὸ ὕδωρ τοῦτο τὸ ἐκπορευόμενον εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν τὴν πρὸς ἀνατολὰς, καὶ κατέβαινεν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἀραβίαν, καὶ ἤρχετο ἕως ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν ἐπὶ τὸ ὕδωρ τῆς διεκβολῆς, καὶ ὑγιάσει τὰ ὕδατα· [And he said to me, This water that goes out into Galilee toward the east, and was going down to Arabia, and came as far as the sea, to the water of the outlet, and will heal the waters] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/EZK47.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/26/47/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/EZK47.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted has אֶל־הַגְּלִילָה הַקַּדְמוֹנָה, “to the eastern region” (גְּלִילָה, a district or circuit, from the same root as the name Galilee), and עַל־הָעֲרָבָה, “down to the Arabah”, the rift valley or steppe. The KJV renders both as common nouns, “east country” and “desert”. The Greek printed at the same verse renders both as place names, Galilee and Arabia, so the two texts present the waters as flowing toward named regions and the KJV as flowing toward unnamed ones.
